headline: Fly By Jing Recalls Creamy Sesame Noodles Due to Possible Peanut Contamination

image.caption: Fly By Jing Recalls Creamy Sesame Noodles Due to Possible Peanut Contamination

description: Fly By Jing voluntarily recalls Creamy Sesame Noodles for potential peanut cross-contact risking allergic reactions. Distributed nationwide, see batch dates to identify.
keywords: Fly By Jing Creamy Sesame Noodles, single packs (NET WT 38 OZ, 107 G) and 4 pack (NET WT 152 OZ, 428 G)

content.subtitle: Quick Answer
content.text: Fly By Jing is voluntarily recalling certain lots of its Creamy Sesame Noodles due to possible cross-contact with peanuts during production. People with peanut allergies should avoid consuming these noodles and check the product's Best By dates to see if their package is affected.

content.subtitle: Recall Summary
content.text:
The recalled product is Fly By Jing Creamy Sesame Noodles available in single packs (NET WT 38 OZ, 107 G) and 4-packs (NET WT 152 OZ, 428 G). These were distributed nationwide through various retailers, including Whole Foods and Thrive Market, as well as online at FlyByJing.com between February 1, 2026, and May 8, 2026.

The recall was initiated after Fly By Jing discovered that a third-party manufacturer used equipment that also processes peanuts when producing these noodles. This cross-contact potentially introduced peanuts into the product, which are not an intended ingredient. The company immediately stopped distribution, alerted customers and retail partners, and placed all remaining inventory on hold.

No other Fly By Jing noodle flavors or sauce products are included in this recall. The affected products can be identified by their Best By dates listed on the back or bottom of the packaging.

People allergic to peanuts should avoid consuming the recalled noodles to prevent potentially hazardous allergic responses.

headline: DOXOrubicin Hydrochloride Liposome Injection recalled for potential glass contamination

image.caption: DOXOrubicin Hydrochloride Liposome Injection recalled for potential glass contamination

description: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries, Inc. recalls one batch of DOXOrubicin Hydrochloride Liposome Injection due to potential glass particles, posing risks if injected.

content.subtitle: Quick Answer
content.text: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries, Inc. is voluntarily recalling one batch of DOXOrubicin Hydrochloride Liposome Injection 50mg/25 mL due to the detection of glass particles in some vials. The recall affects Lot # HAG2581B with expiration May 2027, distributed in the U.S. to hospital and user levels.

content.subtitle: Recall Summary
content.text:
The recalled product is DOXOrubicin Hydrochloride Liposome Injection 50mg/25 mL, used to treat ovarian cancer, AIDS-related Kaposi sarcoma, and multiple myeloma. It is supplied in translucent glass single-dose vials containing red liposomal dispersion. The recall covers a single batch numbered HAG2581B with expiration date 05/31/2027, totaling 675 vials.

The recall stems from the finding of glass particles in some vials during production, which may pose safety risks if injected. Sun Pharma identified the issue, investigated the cause, and has implemented corrective and preventative measures. To date, no adverse events linked to this batch have been reported.

The affected vials were distributed widely across hospitals and user facilities in the United States. Sun Pharma is contacting distributors and customers directly to facilitate return, replacement, or disposal of the recalled product.

content.subtitle: How to Identify the Recalled Product
content.text: The recalled product is identified by the following label details: Brand name "Aisling"; product name "DOXOrubicin Hydrochloride Liposome Injection 50mg/25 mL"; National Drug Code (NDC) 72603-200-01; batch/lot number HAG2581B; expiration date 05/31/2027. Each vial is a 25 mL single-dose glass vial containing a translucent red liposomal dispersion. Checking these exact identifiers on the vial label will confirm whether a product is affected.

content.subtitle: What You Should Do
content.text:
Distributors, hospitals, and users who possess the recalled batch should immediately stop using the affected product. They should arrange to return the recalled vials to the place of purchase or follow instructions from Sun Pharma for return or replacement. Patients who have received this medication should contact their healthcare provider if they experience any health issues potentially related to its use.

For questions or assistance, customers can contact the recall processor, Inmar Inc., at 855-745-9357 (Monday-Friday, 8:30 am to 5:00 pm ET) or via email at rxrecalls@inmar.com. To report adverse events, consumers and healthcare providers may use the FDA’s MedWatch program online or by mail/fax as detailed in the FDA announcement.

content.subtitle: Risk Overview
content.text: Glass particles present in injectable medication can cause harm if administered intravenously. They may lead to local irritation or swelling at the injection site. More serious consequences include blockage of blood vessels, which can result in life-threatening blood clots. Although no reports of injury have been received so far from this batch, the presence of glass presents a significant safety concern warranting removal of the affected product from circulation.

content.subtitle: Who May Be Affected
content.text: Hospitals, healthcare facilities, clinics, and pharmacies that have received Lot # HAG2581B of DOXOrubicin Hydrochloride Liposome Injection 50mg/25 mL should check their inventory immediately. Patients prescribed this medication should confirm with their healthcare providers to ensure their treatment is not affected by the recall.

content.subtitle: Health and Safety Context
content.text: Injectable cancer treatments must be free from particulate contamination to avoid complications such as embolism or inflammatory reactions. Glass shards entering the bloodstream can cause vascular blockages, which may be life-threatening. This recall highlights the importance of strict quality controls in manufacturing sterile injectable drugs to protect patient safety.

headline: Pharmacal Recalls MG217 Multi-Symptom and Eczema Cream Due to Potentially Harmful Bacterial Contamination

image.caption: Pharmacal Recalls MG217 Multi-Symptom and Eczema Cream Due to Potentially Harmful Bacterial Contamination

description: Pharmacal is recalling one lot of MG217 Multi-Symptom Treatment & Eczema Cream nationwide due to contamination with Staphylococcus aureus bacteria.
keywords: Multi-symptom Treatment Cream & Skin Protectant Eczema Cream, 6oz tube

content.subtitle: Quick Answer
content.text: Pharmacal is recalling a specific lot of MG217 Multi-Symptom Treatment Cream & Skin Protectant Eczema Cream because it is contaminated with Staphylococcus aureus, a bacteria that can cause serious infections.

content.subtitle: Recall Summary
content.text:
Pharmacal issued a nationwide recall on May 8, 2026, for one lot of MG217 Multi-Symptom Treatment Cream & Skin Protectant Eczema Cream, packaged in 6oz tubes. This topical cream is intended to relieve symptoms and protect skin affected by eczema.

The recall was initiated after detecting contamination with Staphylococcus aureus bacteria in lot number 1024088, which expires November 2026. Staphylococcus aureus can cause infections if introduced through compromised skin or immune systems.

The recalled product, identified by lot number on the crimped end of the tube and UPC 012277051067, was distributed nationwide to wholesale, retail (including HE BUTT Grocery), and online sellers like Amazon. Pharmacal is contacting distributors to arrange returns and advises consumers to stop use and discard the affected tubes.

facts.product: Multi-symptom Treatment Cream & Skin Protectant Eczema Cream, 6oz tube

content.subtitle: How to Identify the Recalled Product
content.text: Consumers should check their product packaging carefully. The affected MG217 cream comes in a 6oz tube, with product code 5106 and UPC 012277051067. The lot number 1024088 is printed on the crimped end of the tube. Only this specified lot and expiration date (November 2026) are involved in the recall.

content.subtitle: What You Should Do
content.text:
If you have MG217 Multi-Symptom Treatment Cream & Skin Protectant Eczema Cream from lot 1024088, immediately stop using it and safely discard the product. Pharmacal is coordinating returns through its distributors.

Consumers with questions can contact Pharmacal Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Central Time, at 800-558-6614 or email aimho@pharmacalway.com. If you experience any health problems after using this product, contact your healthcare provider promptly.

content.subtitle: Risk Overview
content.text:
The presence of Staphylococcus aureus bacteria in a topical cream is concerning because this bacteria can cause infections ranging from mild skin conditions to severe, potentially life-threatening illnesses such as bloodstream infections or sepsis. Individuals with weakened immune systems or damaged skin—including those with wounds or burns—are particularly vulnerable.

Using contaminated cream could introduce this bacteria to compromised areas, increasing the chance of infection. Although Pharmacal has not yet received reports of illness, the recall is a precaution to prevent infection risks.

content.subtitle: Who May Be Affected
content.text: This recall applies to anyone who has purchased or currently possesses MG217 Multi-Symptom Treatment Cream & Skin Protectant Eczema Cream from lot number 1024088 with expiration in November 2026. Consumers who used the cream and have any health concerns should consult a healthcare provider.

content.subtitle: Health and Safety Context
content.text: Topical creams contaminated with bacteria like Staphylococcus aureus pose a risk because damaged skin can allow bacteria to enter the body and cause infections. People with eczema or other skin conditions may have skin barriers that are compromised, increasing susceptibility. Proper hygiene and careful inspection of skin products help minimize risks.

content.subtitle: Quick Answer
content.text: XD Investments LLC has voluntarily recalled all lots of Better Weather Fix Elixir dietary supplements due to the presence of undeclared Mitragynine and Mitragynine Pseudoindoxyl, compounds derived from kratom that can cause serious and potentially fatal health effects.

content.subtitle: Recall Summary
content.text:
Better Weather Fix Elixir products, sold as dietary supplements by XD Investments LLC of Houston, TX, are being recalled because FDA testing detected the undeclared presence of Mitragynine and Mitragynine Pseudoindoxyl (MP), active components derived from kratom. MP is a more potent chemical related to Mitragynine and carries heightened risks.

The recall covers approximately 448 boxes of Better Weather Fix Elixir products, including all flavors and variations such as "Better Weather Fix Elixir Berry." These products were sold online through xdeor.com and maxensupplements.com from around November 9, 2025, to March 28, 2026. Sales and distribution stopped on April 1, 2026, with remaining stock removed from the market.

To date, there have been no reports of adverse health events linked to these products. Consumers are advised to stop use immediately and contact the company for refund details or further help.

content.subtitle: How to Identify the Recalled Product
content.text: Consumers can identify the recalled products by checking the packaging for the label names "Better Weather Fix Elixir" or "Better Weather Fix Elixir Berry." The recall includes all flavors and lot numbers sold in display boxes. Since lot numbers are not specified in the FDA notice, consumers should refer to the product labeling and their purchase date on xdeor.com or maxensupplements.com to confirm if their product falls within the sale period from November 9, 2025, to March 28, 2026.

content.subtitle: What You Should Do
content.text:
Consumers who have Better Weather Fix Elixir products should immediately stop using them. The products can be disposed of safely or returned to XD Investments LLC for a refund or further instructions.

For assistance, consumers can contact XD Investments LLC at (832) 449-6471 or via email at info@xdeor.com. If anyone experiences adverse health effects potentially related to the product, they should seek medical advice promptly.

content.subtitle: Risk Overview
content.text: Mitragynine and Mitragynine Pseudoindoxyl are compounds found in kratom, known to affect the central nervous system. Consumption can lead to a range of symptoms including nausea, vomiting, increased heart rate, palpitations, hallucinations, sedation, anxiety, and loss of consciousness. headline: Jonco Industries recalls Williams Sonoma and Fireworks Popcorn White Cheddar Seasoning for Salmonella risk

image.caption: Jonco Industries recalls Williams Sonoma and Fireworks Popcorn White Cheddar Seasoning for Salmonella risk

description: Jonco Industries recalls certain White Cheddar Seasoning products due to possible Salmonella contamination. Consumers should check lot codes and avoid use.

content.subtitle: Quick Answer
content.text: Jonco Industries is recalling select consumer-sized White Cheddar Seasoning products because they may be contaminated with Salmonella, a bacteria that can cause infections. Consumers who have purchased these products should check the lot codes and not consume them.

content.subtitle: Recall Summary
content.text:
Jonco Industries, Inc., based in Milwaukee, WI, has announced a recall of certain consumer-sized White Cheddar Seasoning products. These seasonings are sold under the Williams Sonoma and Fireworks Popcorn brands and were distributed in limited quantities through retail stores.

The recall stems from a potential Salmonella contamination identified in an upstream milk powder ingredient supplied by California Dairies, Inc., which was used in making these seasoning products. The affected products include White Cheddar Seasoning sold in specific formats, each marked with distinct lot codes printed on their packaging.

No illnesses linked to this recall have been reported to date. Upon notification by its supplier, JCB Flavors, Jonco Industries immediately stopped distribution, informed customers, and placed remaining inventory on hold to prevent further exposure.

content.subtitle: How to Identify the Recalled Product
content.text:
Check the product packaging for the following details:

  • Brand: Williams Sonoma (Popcorn Sampler Gift Box containing White Cheddar Seasoning) or Fireworks Popcorn (Poppings & Toppings gift set or 1.6 oz White Cheddar Seasoning jars)
  • Lot codes printed on the packaging are key identifiers. The affected lot codes are: 088594-2-1 for Williams Sonoma Popcorn Sampler Gift Box; 088594-5-1 for Fireworks Popcorn Poppings & Toppings gift set; and 088594-7-1 for Fireworks White Cheddar Seasoning 1.6 oz jars.

Product labels submitted to the FDA provide reference images if further verification is needed.

content.subtitle: What You Should Do
content.text: Consumers with the recalled White Cheddar Seasoning should not consume the product. Instead, they should return it to the original place of purchase for a full refund. If you have questions or need additional information, contact Jonco Industries at 414-449-2000 during normal business hours.

content.subtitle: Risk Overview
content.text:
Salmonella is a bacteria that can cause serious illness, especially in young children, elderly individuals, and those with weakened immune systems. Infection may result in symptoms like fever, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. While healthy individuals often recover without complications, Salmonella can sometimes cause severe conditions if it spreads to the bloodstream or other parts of the body.

Since White Cheddar Seasoning is a food product ingested directly or used on snacks, contamination could lead to foodborne illness if consumed. Avoiding affected products is important to reduce this risk.

content.subtitle: Who May Be Affected
content.text: Consumers who have purchased White Cheddar Seasoning products under the Williams Sonoma or Fireworks Popcorn brands—particularly those sold in consumer-sized packaging with the specified lot codes—should carefully check their products. Retail customers of stores that carried these items, including West Allis Cheese and Sausage, are encouraged to verify if their products are affected.

content.subtitle: Health and Safety Context
content.text:
Foodborne pathogens such as Salmonella can contaminate powdered milk ingredients and other dry food products, which makes careful monitoring critical in food manufacturing. When seasoning products are contaminated, they pose a risk because they are sprinkled on ready-to-eat foods and not cooked further, potentially allowing bacteria to infect consumers.

Good food safety practices include checking for recalls regularly and adhering to guidance when contamination is identified to prevent illness.

keywords: Potential to be contaminated with Clostridium botulinum.

content.subtitle: Quick Answer
content.text: Shining Sea Fish Co. is recalling Ma Cohen’s Kippered Herring because the product may be contaminated with Clostridium botulinum due to uneviscerated fish. This bacterium can cause a serious, potentially fatal illness called botulism.

content.subtitle: Recall Summary
content.text:
Shining Sea Fish Co., based in Detroit, MI, has issued a recall for its catch weight packages of Ma Cohen’s Kippered Herring smoked fish. The recall was announced after routine testing by the Minnesota Department of Agriculture found the fish had not been fully eviscerated. Because the fish are longer than five inches and uneviscerated, there is a risk of contamination with Clostridium botulinum, a bacterium that can cause life-threatening botulism.

The recalled products were sold in retail grocery stores across Michigan, Minnesota, and North Dakota. They are packaged in clear plastic with a foil label showing the product name, lot numbers on the back, and expiration dates either printed on the package or added by stores on stickers. Specific recalled lot numbers include 25079 (expiring May 03, 2026), 25055 (May 12, 2026), 25028 (June 03, 2026), and 26344 (July 22, 2026). No illnesses have been reported in connection with this recall to date.

The company has permanently discontinued this product and urges consumers who purchased Ma Cohen’s Kippered Herring to return it to their place of purchase for a full refund. For further inquiries, consumers may contact Shining Sea Fish Co. during business hours.

If consumers have questions, they can contact Shining Sea Fish Co. at 1-313-542-2637, Monday through Friday, 9:00 am to 3:00 pm EST.

content.subtitle: Risk Overview
content.text: Clostridium botulinum produces a toxin that causes botulism, a rare but serious illness. Consuming food contaminated with this toxin can lead to muscle weakness, breathing difficulties, and can be fatal if untreated. Botulism symptoms include general weakness, dizziness, double vision, difficulty speaking or swallowing, and in severe cases, respiratory failure. Because Kippered Herring was found to be uneviscerated, spores of this bacterium may survive and grow under certain conditions, increasing health risks. Therefore, avoiding consumption of this product is important to prevent potential botulism poisoning.

The recalled muffins come in 9-count, 6-ounce packages bearing the lot code 6082 with a military time stamp and UPC 811070033979, distributed on March 31, 2026. The product was shipped through a third-party distributor, potentially reaching retail and food service locations.

headline: Voluntary Recall of George J. Howe Co. Sunflower Seeds for Undeclared Tree Nut (Cashew) Allergens

image.caption: Voluntary Recall of George J. Howe Co. Sunflower Seeds for Undeclared Tree Nut (Cashew) Allergens

description: George J. Howe Co. recalls sunflower seeds sold in multiple states due to undeclared cashew allergens, posing risk to individuals with tree nut allergies.

content.subtitle: Quick Answer
content.text: George J. Howe Co. is voluntarily recalling sunflower seeds because they may contain undeclared cashew tree nuts, which can cause serious allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

content.subtitle: Recall Summary
content.text:
George J. Howe Co., located in Grove City, Pennsylvania, has announced a voluntary recall of approximately 13,619 pounds of sunflower seeds. This action follows the discovery that some products contain undeclared tree nut allergens, specifically cashews.

The recalled sunflower seeds were distributed across multiple U.S. states, including Alabama, Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Iowa, Illinois, Indiana, Kansas, Kentucky, Maryland, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Mississippi, North Carolina, New Jersey, Ohio, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Virginia, and Wisconsin. Distribution channels included retail grocery chains, foodservice accounts, specialty retailers, concession and airport operators, and institutional customers.

The recall was initiated after a routine inspection revealed packaging omissions for the cashew allergen, caused by a production process oversight during product changeover. No illnesses related to this issue have been reported.

content.subtitle: How to Identify the Recalled Product
content.text:
The recalled sunflower seed products can be identified by their packaging and label details as follows:

  • Plastic Stand-Up Pouch, 11 oz, Blue packaging with the brand name "SUNFLOWER SEEDS" and product names "Fresh Roasted Sunflower Seeds, Lightly Salted" or "Fresh Roasted Sunflower Seeds, No Salt"
  • Specific UPCs and Best By dates apply:
    • Lightly Salted: UPC 073171003163, Best By dates 08/28/2026, 09/18/2026, 10/01/2026, 10/09/2026, 11/18/2026, 12/12/2026
    • No Salt: UPC 073171003200, Best By dates 09/24/2026, 10/30/2026, 11/18/2026, 12/11/2026
  • Plastic Tub, 9.5 oz, Gold label with product name "Sunflower Seeds, roasted and salted." UPC 073171027015 and Best By dates 07/22/2026 and 09/05/2026

All recalled products include an allergen warning stating the product was packaged in a facility processing peanuts, tree nuts, milk products, soy, wheat, and eggs, but they omit the specific presence of cashews.

content.subtitle: What You Should Do
content.text:
Consumers who have purchased any of the recalled sunflower seed products matching the descriptions, UPC codes, and dates listed should not consume them if they have a cashew or tree nut allergy. Instead, they are advised to return the product to the place of purchase for a full refund.

For additional questions or concerns, consumers can contact George J. Howe Company customer service at (800) 367-4693, Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. EST, or via email at quality@georgehowe.com.

content.subtitle: Risk Overview
content.text: Tree nut allergies, such as those to cashews, can trigger severe or potentially life-threatening reactions in allergic individuals even at very low exposure levels. Undeclared allergens on food packaging represent a significant risk, as affected consumers may unknowingly consume the product. For those without a tree nut allergy, the sunflower seeds are safe to eat.

content.subtitle: Who May Be Affected
content.text: Consumers who have purchased George J. Howe Co. sunflower seeds and have a known allergy or sensitivity to tree nuts, specifically cashews, should check their products carefully. Those without such allergies are not at risk from this recall.

content.subtitle: Health and Safety Context
content.text: Food allergies to tree nuts are among the most common and potentially severe food allergies in the United States. Even trace amounts of an allergen can provoke life-threatening reactions, such as anaphylaxis. Accurate labeling is critical for consumer safety, enabling allergic individuals to avoid exposure. This recall highlights the importance of verifying allergen information on packaging and the vigilance needed during food production to prevent cross-contamination.
